title: useHash:true makes it render slower.
body:
If I use the _useHash_ option under _urlSync_, the results renderization gets really slow.

Here's **without** _useHash_:
![without useHash](http://g.recordit.co/A1n7bNNLN7.gif)
(video: http://recordit.co/A1n7bNNLN7)

And **with** _useHash_:
![with useHash](http://g.recordit.co/8bxwVUGy9B.gif)
(video: http://recordit.co/8bxwVUGy9B)

comments.body: Hi @semeano, is the "without useHash" case still using urlSynchronisation? Indeed it may be that in some situations, updating the hash too often leads to bad performance.

Hi @vvo,

Yes, it is still using urlSync.
The only difference between those two is just the useHash flag.
@semeano Which browser are you using for your tests? On which platform / OS?

Sorry, should have mentioned in the first post.

Chrome 54.0.2840.71 (64-bit)
Mac OS X 10.9.5 (Mavericks)
Just a suggestion. Instead of updating the url on every keystroke, why not use the urlSync.threshold parameter to affect the url updating time too?

> Just a suggestion. Instead of updating the url on every keystroke, why not use the urlSync.threshold parameter to affect the url updating time too?

It's tricky, because then you have an interface that gets updated at every keystroke but the url itself is only updated after 700ms, which results in a visual distraction if you already started reading the webpage (we tried it, not convincing).

Can I ask you the reason for using the hash instead of the url? Ultimately I think we will remove the hash option because it causes too much issues.

I was having some issues. Sometimes if I went back to the results page (i.e. homepage > results page > product page > back to results page), the url would stop sync.

But right now I'm not using urlSync anymore.

We'd better try to fix those non working urlSync classical issues before we try to fix the performance of the hash based one that we will eventually drop support of.

If you are able to reproduce the issue, please open a new one, thanks a lot
